label: Formal object of a bearer's favouring: the ranking that measures its kind of operation
term: formal object of a bearer's favouring (obj b φ)
definition: A formal-object assignment obj gives, for each bearer b and favouring profile φ, a ranking of candidates in each variation scenario: the standard by which b's favouring φ is measured (lane P's per-bearer reading of the standard of favouring). It is intended as the formal object of b's kind of operation: for a will (rational appetite) the good, read as the value order; for a natural tendency the end of the nature, which may be an end content D or, on the imitability-exemplar account, the good. It is indexed by the bearer because one profile can belong to bearers of different kinds: Lane 2b's D-directed nature and determined will are the same function fitOrder, measured by D-realization for the natural bearer and by the good for the willing one (appetiteGrid, last row). It is not the favouring's particular content: with obj b φ := φ every favouring would trivially make exactly its object's verdicts, and that reading is not intended. Example: a one-domain knower is measured by truth, the object of knowing as such, not by the truths of its domain. In Lean the assignment is a parameter; nothing in the type stops a degenerate assignment, so this record states the intended constraint.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 lane H3), attribution deferred. It is a parameter of PureFavouringTracksItsObject and ActualRootFavouringObjectIsValue and has no Lean declaration of its own. The per-bearer reading was introduced and tested in lane P (docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'When is a restriction of content a limitation?', A4). See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Natural or rational appetite? The purity premises and the object of an original source's favouring'.
